text: Sir, I have read every line of the Principia, twice, and I shall thank you not to interrupt me again. Observe the apple. It falls, as it has always fallen, and I see no reason to apologise for it.

voices.deepbass: A proud English man of about sixty-five with a very deep, resonant bass-baritone voice, slow and grave, with a precise upper-class Received Pronunciation accent, like a stern Victorian judge delivering a verdict.
voices.gravelly: A proud English man of about sixty-five with a low, rough, gravelly voice and a clipped, formal British accent, speaking in short firm phrases, like an old army colonel correcting a recruit.
voices.fussy: A proud English man of about sixty-five with a thin, high-pitched, nasal voice, quick, fussy and precise, with a refined British accent, like an indignant old clerk who cannot bear being contradicted.
